item.title: Spectroscopic Investigation of 5-FU Association at Chitosan-Stabilized Au Nanoparticle Interfaces
item.description:
Abstract
Chitosan-stabilized gold nanoparticles (Au NPs-Chi) are candidate carriers for combined chemo-photothermal therapy because of their tunable surface properties and ability to incorporate therapeutic molecules. Understanding how formulation parameters influence interfacial organization and the chemical environment of the polymer-rich interfaces is important for controlling drug-nanocarrier interactions and for designing Au NPs-Chi as chemo-photothermal drug carriers. In this study, Au NPs-Chi loaded with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) were prepared using different gold precursor and chitosan concentrations to investigate how formulation composition affects nanoparticle morphology, interfacial chemistry, and 5-FU association and retention. The systems were characterized by STEM, UV–vis, ATR-FTIR, and XPS. Mean STEM diameters ranged from 9.1 ± 0.2 nm (15Au-1Chi) to 22.0 ± 7.0 nm (10Au-0.5Chi), the LSPR band appeared at 527–534 nm, and all suspensions exhibited positive zeta potentials of +48 to +62 mV. Formulations prepared with the intermediate precursor concentration showed the most uniform nanoparticle morphology. Spectroscopic investigations indicated that 5-FU-associated changes occurred primarily within the chitosan-rich interfacial layer, while no clear evidence of a dominant direct interaction with the metallic Au core was observed. Fluorine from 5-FU (F 1s, 0.6–1.5 at %) was detected in all loaded samples and was absent from the unloaded formulations. End-point free-drug measurements under physiological saline conditions revealed formulation- and loading-time-dependent variations in the detectable free 5-FU fraction, with normalized ratios ranging from 0.5 to 1.8 relative to the 1 h value. After 1 h of incubation, 8–25% of the added 5-FU was detected in the medium. For the 15Au-1Chi formulation loaded for 4 h, the normalized free-drug ratio remained between approximately 1.0 and 1.2 over the investigated incubation period. These results relate formulation composition to the chemical environment of 5-FU in the chitosan-rich interfacial layer and provide physicochemical information relevant to the further development of Au NPs-Chi systems for combined chemo-photothermal applications.

item.title: Innovative Process for Cellulose Acetate Recovery from Cigarette Butts by Means of Natural Deep Eutectic Solvents
item.description:
Abstract
This work investigated a waste product of environmental concern, cigarette butts, as a potential source of cellulose acetate. It is estimated that there are 967 million smokers worldwide who produce approximately 6 trillion cigarette butts each year, causing a direct environmental impact. The proposed approach aimed to transform this polluting waste into a high-value material, recovering pure cellulose acetate from cigarette butts for reuse in a variety of applications. Developing an effective and environmentally friendly recovery method was very challenging. This was achieved by using different types of natural deep eutectic solvents (DES), which are a class of innovative solvents that combine the properties of ionic liquids and organic solvents. They are known for their sustainability and versatility. The efficiency of the various DES employed was evaluated using thermogravimetric analysis, nuclear magnetic resonance, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy and Fourier-transform infrared analysis. Based on the results obtained, the most effective DES was identified as that consisting of choline chloride and levulinic acid, which allows clean cellulose acetate to be recovered with a yield of up to 93%.

item.title: Full Pore System Characteristics, Fractal Dimensions, and Controlling Factors of Lacustrine Laminated Shale: Implications for Shale Oil Reservoirs in the Liaohe Depression, NE China
item.description:
Abstract
Clarifying the pore system of unconventional oil and gas reservoirs is essential for understanding hydrocarbon accumulation, improving recovery efficiency, and accurately assessing resource potential. However, research on pore systems in lacustrine shales remains limited, largely because the development of diverse laminas produces strong heterogeneity. In the current research, 20 samples from the fourth member of the Shahejie Formation in the Western Sag, Liaohe Depression of the Bohai Bay Basin were systematically characterized through a combined approach that includes CO2 adsorption, N2 adsorption, and high-pressure mercury intrusion (HPMI) experiments. Fractal dimensions for micropores (D1), mesopores (D2), and macropores (D3) were obtained using the V–S model for CO2 adsorption, the FHH model for N2 adsorption, and the MSP model for HPMI. The results demonstrate that the laminated shale is composed of light-colored layers rich in quartz, feldspar, calcite, and dolomite, which often alternate with darker layers primarily consisting of clay minerals and organic matter. The pore system of the laminated shale consists mainly of intergranular pores, intercrystalline pores, dissolution pores, and microfractures within the matrix, excluding pores associated with organic matter. In terms of pore volume, the pore system is primarily characterized by mesopores and macropores, while micropores significantly contribute to the specific surface area. The fractal dimensions are observed to range from 2.565 to 2.880 for D1, 2.458 to 2.659 for D2, and 2.929 to 2.999 for D3. This indicates that macropores display the greatest heterogeneity, followed by micropores, with mesopores being comparatively homogeneous. Correlation analysis indicates a strong positive relationship between D1 and both the micropore specific surface area and the pore volume of micropores. The correlation is influenced by the total organic carbon (TOC) content, thermal maturity (Ro), and clay mineral content. While D2 demonstrates a positive correlation with mesopore parameters, its overall heterogeneity remains relatively low due to compaction-induced homogenization. D3 is mainly affected by the dissolution of carbonates and the presence of microfracture networks, often reaching the theoretical upper limit in the majority of samples. The composition of minerals has a varying impact based on scale: clay minerals facilitate the formation of micropores and mesopores; felsic minerals contribute moderately to the volumes of mesopores and macropores; carbonate minerals encourage the formation of irregular dissolution pores, which in turn enhances D3. Within the low-mature to mature oil window (Ro = 0.65–1.00%), the pore system is predominantly controlled by the diagenetic evolution of the mineral matrix rather than organic matter pores. This research presents a quantitative framework for characterizing the complete pore system in laminated shale and provides insights for reservoir evaluation in lacustrine shale oil systems.

item.title: Comparative One-Step Activation of Zhundong Coal Using KOH and ZnCl 2 : Hierarchically Porous Adsorbents for Malachite Green Adsorption
item.description:
Abstract
Although abundant in reserves, Zhundong coal is prone to severe slagging when combusted due to its high sodium content. Converting this coal into functionally designed carbon materials offers a sustainable strategy for clean utilization. This study compared hierarchically porous adsorbents prepared from Zhundong coal by one-step activation with ZnCl2 or KOH (denoted as ZnCl2@coal and KOH@coal, respectively) in terms of their pore structures and malachite green (MG) adsorption behavior in model aqueous solutions. Characterization revealed increased carbon content (from 67% to approximately 83%), specific surface area (from 10 to 1210–1773 m2/g), and pore volume of up to 1.00 cm3/g in both ZnCl2@coal and KOH@coal relative to the raw Zhundong coal. Adsorption experiments demonstrated that both adsorbents removed MG over the investigated pH range (2–9) and KCl concentrations (0–1000 mmol/L). The adsorption kinetics were well described by the pseudo-second-order model, whereas the Langmuir model fitted the equilibrium data better than the Freundlich model. Thermodynamic analysis indicated favorable MG adsorption under the adopted standard-state treatment and suggested a possible endothermic trend. At 308 K, the highest measured MG adsorption capacity of ZnCl2@coal was 5252.7 mg/g at an initial concentration of 6000 mg/L, while the Langmuir-derived maximum capacity was 8522.5 mg/g. Its higher MG uptake relative to KOH@coal at high initial concentrations was associated with a greater mesopore surface area and larger average pore width (2.77 nm versus 2.25 nm), although differences in surface chemistry and residual inorganic species may also contribute. This study provides a comparative assessment of KOH and ZnCl2 activation for converting low-grade Zhundong coal into porous adsorbents, highlighting the differences in the resulting materials’ physicochemical properties and MG adsorption behavior.

item.title: FluoVolt Staining Compromises Cell Viability and Morphology during Live-Cell Voltage Imaging
item.description:
Abstract
Fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes (VSDs) enable noninvasive, high-throughput optical monitoring of membrane potential in live cells but may introduce unintended experimental effects that complicate data interpretation. To address this, a key challenge is to characterize and minimize staining- and imaging-associated perturbations to optimize their reliable use across different cell types and imaging conditions. In this study, we systematically evaluate the VSD FluoVolt, its photobleaching, and its effects on cell viability, detachment, and morphology in cancer cell lines (GIN31 and SK-MEL-30) and primary human macrophages. Time-course imaging revealed cell-type-dependent photobleaching, with SK-MEL-30 cells exhibiting rapid fluorescence decay during imaging compared with other cell types. FluoVolt staining combined with excitation was associated with significant cell detachment in GIN31 and SK-MEL-30 cells and with reduced viability accompanied by pronounced morphological changes in GIN31 cells, characterized by a shift from an elongated to an amoeboid-like phenotype. Notably, morphological alterations were observed even in the absence of excitation, indicating that FluoVolt staining alone was also associated with measurable changes in cell morphology. Optimization of staining conditions using reduced dye and loading solution concentrations and incubation time significantly reduced these effects while maintaining measurable fluorescence. Collectively, these findings further characterize the effects associated with FluoVolt staining under the experimental conditions tested, highlight their dependence on cell type and imaging conditions, and emphasize the importance of protocol optimization for the reliable application of FluoVolt in live-cell imaging.

item.title: Heparin- and Selenocystamine-Functionalized Silk Fibroin Hydrogel for Anticoagulation and Catalytic Nitric Oxide Generation
item.description:
Abstract
Thrombosis and restenosis remain major challenges for vascular implants, motivating the development of biomaterials that integrate anticoagulant activity with complementary vascular biofunctions. Here, a dual-functionalized silk fibroin (SF)-based hydrogel was developed via a one-pot 1-ethyl-3-(3-(dimethylamino)propyl)carbodiimide (EDC)/N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS)-mediated conjugation of heparin and selenocystamine (SeCA). The resulting SF-heparin-SeCA conjugate can be further cross-linked into a hydrogel network through enzymatic dityrosine formation under mild, room-temperature conditions. Within the hydrogel, heparin provides anticoagulant activity, while SeCA catalyzes nitric oxide (NO) generation from ph ysiological S-nitrosothiol donors, such as S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO), thereby integrating complementary anticoagulant and NO-generating functions within a single SF-based platform. The hydrogel exhibited distinct physicochemical and mechanical properties, sustained NO-generating capability, and enhanced anticoagulant performance. Collectively, these findings establish a streamlined strategy for integrating anticoagulant and NO-generating functions within an SF-based hydrogel and support its potential for blood-contacting vascular applications.

item.title: GNPS Molecular-Networking-Guided Isolation of New Antiphotoaging Theasaponins from Camellia chekiangoleosa Flower
item.description:
Abstract
Guided by the global natural products social molecular networking (GNPS) technology, a targeted phytochemical investigation on the flowers of Camellia chekiangoleosa was performed, yielding two new naturally occurring theasaponins and four new related artifacts named camelliosides K–P (1, 2, 5, 6, 9, and 13), together with eight known analogues. The chemical structures were systematically elucidated based on comprehensive NMR and MS spectroscopic analyses, combined with hydrolysis experiments for sugar moiety identification. Structurally, camellioside K (1) had a rare ketone substitution at the C-11 position, while compound 2 represents an unusual trisaccharide saponin that is rarely reported from the Theaceae family, significantly enriching the structural diversity of plant saponins derived from Camellia species. All isolated compounds exerted prominent anti-inflammatory effects by remarkably inhibiting the production of pro-inflammatory TNF-α and IL-6. Further In vitro antiphotoaging assay demonstrated that the new compounds 1 and 2 exerted remarkable protective effects against ultraviolet B (UVB)-induced photoaging damage in human fibroblasts. Both compounds markedly upregulated the production of type I collagen and downregulated the mRNA expression of matrix metalloproteinases 1 (Mmp1) and 3 (Mmp3). Notably, camelliosides K and L were verified to promote the biogenesis of mitophagosomes and lysosomes, activate PINK1–Parkin signaling consistent with a mitophagy-related response, and alleviate mitochondrial damage by elevating the protein levels of PINK1 and Parkin in UVB-stimulated fibroblasts. Collectively, this work demonstrates that the newly identified saponins from C. chekiangoleosa serve as promising natural candidates for the prevention and treatment of skin inflammation and UV-triggered photoaging diseases.

item.title: Potential Involvement of Collagen in Skin Chemiexcitation
item.description:
Abstract
Chemiexcitation is the formation of electronically excited states through oxidative reactions, in which biomolecules such as lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, or pigments are oxidized by reactive oxygen species. The electronically excited states may transfer excitation energy to nearby biomolecules or emit ultraweak photons. Chemiexcitation has been most convincingly demonstrated in pigments (melanin oxidation) and lipids (lipid peroxidation), whereas only limited evidence suggests that protein oxidation may contribute to this process. In this study, we investigated the potential contribution of collagen oxidation to chemiexcitation in UV-exposed skin. Imaging of ultraweak photon emission revealed a sustained increase following UV irradiation, which correlated with the formation of collagen carbonyls. In addition, the formation of oxidized tryptophan derivatives, including kynurenine, is consistent with the involvement of tryptophan oxidation in the observed photon emission. Together, these findings suggest that oxidative modification of collagen, particularly of tryptophan, may contribute to chemiexcitation in the skin. The exploration of chemiexcitation associated with collagen oxidation expands the current understanding of oxidative processes in skin and may contribute to the development of more effective photoprotective strategies.

item.title: From Chemistry to Biology: Zinc(II)–1,10-Phenanthroline-5,6-dione Complex Exhibits Potent Activity against Mammalian Stages of Trypanosoma cruzi with Controlled Host Cell Toxicity
item.description:
Abstract
Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, affects 6–7 million people worldwide and causes ∼12,000 deaths annually. Treatments are limited to benznidazole and nifurtimox, both associated with toxicity, adverse effects, and frequent treatment discontinuation, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Here, a coordination compound was synthesized and evaluated against cell-derived trypomastigotes and intracellular amastigotes of T. cruzi. The compound, [Zn(1,10-phenanthroline-5,6-dione)3](ClO4)2·6H2O (Zn-phendione), consists of a hexacoordinated Zn(II) center bound to three phendione ligands, forming a dicationic complex. The anti-T. cruzi activity of Zn-phendione was initially evaluated in trypomastigotes, in which it reduced parasite viability in a dose-dependent manner after 24 h, with an LD50 of 3.30 nM. This activity was higher than that of the free ligand phendione (LD50 = 7.56 nM) and was 388-fold greater than benznidazole (LD50 = 1,280 nM), whereas the zinc salt alone showed no activity. Zn-phendione-treated trypomastigotes, as observed by optical and scanning electron microscopy, exhibited pronounced morphological alterations, including cell twisting, swelling, and partial or complete loss of the unique flagellum. Notably, 1-h exposure to Zn-phendione decreased trypomastigote infectivity by ∼50% at the LD50. Moreover, Zn-phendione dose-dependently inhibited intracellular amastigote replication after 72 h (IC50 = 36 nM), outperforming benznidazole (IC50 = 210 nM), while showing no toxicity to the host cells used for amastigote maintenance. For trypomastigotes, 24-h exposure resulted in selectivity index (SI) values of >312.5 for benznidazole and 64,800 for Zn-phendione, whereas for amastigotes, 72-h exposure yielded SI values of >238.1 and 83.3, respectively. These findings highlight Zn-phendione as a promising candidate for the development of new therapeutic strategies against T. cruzi.

item.title: Ignition Theoretical Prediction Model for Aircraft Fuel Tanks Impacted by Polymer-Based Reactive Materials
item.description:
Abstract
Reactive fragment Al/W/PTFE is a novel polymer-based composite material, which is mainly applied to impact aircraft fuel tanks. The coupled kinetic-chemical energy damage of Al/W/PTFE makes the damage process of the aircraft fuel tank ignition extremely complex. Currently, there is no comprehensive model to predict the outcome of ignition damage. In this study, an ignition theoretical prediction model was first established. First, based on the comprehensive temperature rise of reactive fragments and an improved Avrami-Erofeev equation incorporating the proposed nonlinear reaction rate, a new computational model was developed. Second, considering the fuel characteristics of RP-3 kerosene and calculating the state parameters and the temperature rise of the ullage layer in the tank, an ignition theoretical prediction model accounting for the coupled kinetic-chemical energy damage of reactive fragments was established. Finally, impact ignition damage tests were conducted in which reactive fragments impacted an aircraft’s equivalent fuel tank, and the model’s accuracy was verified against experimental results. The research results show that the theoretical ignition critical velocity of a reactive fragment impacting the ullage layer of a nonfull fuel tank ranges from 520.00 to 535.59 m/s, with an error of 2.67% to 5.74% compared to experimental data (506.49 m/s). The model calculates a theoretical autoignition velocity of 877.19 m/s for RP-3, which aligns with experimental observations of violent combustion occurring at impact velocities exceeding 810 m/s. A single ignition delay curve cannot accurately predict the ignition results of reactive fragments impacting the fuel tank. The research will directly guide the design application of a fuel system protection for military/civilian aircraft and also provide an applied basis for the engineering evaluation of the lethality of polymer-based reactive materials based on chemical effects.

item.title: Low-Barrier H 2 Dissociation on the Al 9 Sc 4 – Nanocluster: Superatomic Shell Effects and Implications for Low-Temperature Hydrogen Activation
item.description:
Abstract
Low-temperature activation of the H–H bond on nonprecious, lightweight materials is a key elementary step for hydrogen technologies, including hydrogen storage and hydrogenation catalysis. This study systematically investigates the hydrogen adsorption and dissociation properties of bimetallic anionic nanoclusters [AlxScy–] (x + y = 13) using density functional theory. Our results demonstrate that substituting Al atoms with Sc atoms significantly stabilizes the dissociatively adsorbed hydrogen state and enhances the reactivity toward H–H bond cleavage. Upon hydrogen adsorption, the cluster geometries remain largely intact and preferentially undergo dissociative chemisorption, as evidenced by dissociative adsorption energies and negative Gibbs free energies of adsorption for all Sc-containing clusters, whereas the molecularly adsorbed precursors are endergonic. For the first H2 molecule, the Al9Sc4– cluster exhibits a submerged-barrier dissociation pathway: the transition state TS1 lies 0.04 eV below the separated reactants but 0.07 eV above the molecularly adsorbed precursor, so that H–H cleavage is nearly activationless on the electronic-energy scale. In contrast, other [AlxScy–] clusters exhibit TS1 energies of 0.04 to 1.25 eV relative to the separated reactants, while pure Al13– exhibits a substantially higher barrier of 1.45 eV. However, the dissociated product is strongly stabilized (−1.61 eV; ΔG = −1.30 eV), so that the reverse recombination/desorption barrier amounts to 1.57 eV (1.51 eV in free energy); the molecular adsorption of additional H2 molecules is slightly endothermic and the dissociation barriers rise to 1.28 and 1.48 eV for the fourth and fifth H2; and the gravimetric capacity at the highest loading considered is 2.33 wt %. Electronic-structure analysis suggests that the two localized Sc 3d electrons of bare Al9Sc4– (1S21P61D102S22P61F123d2) facilitate charge transfer to H2 and, together with the two H 1s electrons, complete a delocalized 42-electron superatomic shell (1S21P61D102S22P61F143S2) in Al9Sc4–@2H, which destabilizes the H–H bond while strongly stabilizing the resulting metal-H bonds, whereas the availability of Sc–Sc bridge sites and the local cluster geometry also contribute to the barrier trend. These results identify Al9Sc4– as a model system for low-temperature H2 activation and provide electronic-structure design principles for Al-based clusters for H2 activation, while showing that the same shell completion that facilitates H–H cleavage also hinders hydrogen release, so that a submerged dissociation barrier alone does not guarantee reversible hydrogen storage.

item.title: Phenethylamine-Derived β-Lactam Derivatives as Antibacterial Leads against Respiratory Pathogens: In Vitro Evaluation, Cytotoxicity Profiling, and In Silico Insights
item.description:
Abstract
Secondary pulmonary bacterial infections represent a severe clinical complication in lung cancer management, necessitating effective antibacterial strategies. In this study, a series of phenethylamine-derived imines (1–6) and their cyclized β-lactam derivatives (7–12) were systematically evaluated as prospective antibacterial leads against respiratory pathogens (Klebsiella pneumoniae and Streptococcus pneumoniae), alongside cytotoxicity profiling in A549 human lung cells. Phenotypic antibacterial assays showed that open-chain imine precursors (1–6) had no discernible activity, whereas core cyclization into β-lactam derivatives (7–12) conferred antibacterial activity (MIC: 12.5–50 μM), including activity against K. pneumoniae, which showed no inhibition zone with ampicillin. Compounds 7 and 11 had the lowest MICs against K. pneumoniae (12.5 μM). Comparing MIC values with A549 cytotoxicity gave an in vitro selectivity index (SI) of >16 for compound 7 against K. pneumoniae. This is a censored lower bound (A549 IC50 > 200 μM) that reflects low cytotoxicity in a lung cell line and does not indicate cancer selectivity. Preliminary molecular docking against bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and human MDM2 gave scores that differed little among compounds and did not follow the MIC values, so they are treated here as exploratory only. Overall, these findings identify phenethylamine-derived β-lactams as a scaffold for antibacterial lead development that warrants further mechanistic investigation and testing in noncancerous lung cells.

item.title: Competitive Adsorption of Pb(II), Zn(II), and Cr(III) on a Chitosan–Graphene Oxide Biocomposite: Experimental and DFT Insights
item.description:
Abstract
A chitosan–graphene oxide (Cs/GO) biocomposite was evaluated for Pb(II), Zn(II), and Cr(III) removal using adsorption experiments, adsorbent-free controls, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The composite exhibited a predominantly amorphous, mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 180.0 m2 g–1 and oxygen- and nitrogen-containing functional groups. Pb(II) uptake showed an apparent plateau from the first sampling point at 5 min. In competitive solutions containing 100 mg L–1 of each metal at pH 4.5, apparent distribution coefficients after 60 min followed Pb(II) > Cr(III) > Zn(II), with Pb/Cr and Pb/Zn separation factors of 8.9 and 27.5, respectively. Adsorbent-free controls showed 99.34% Cr(III) loss at pH 7.0, compared with 5.22% at pH 4.5, demonstrating the importance of distinguishing adsorption from pH-induced metal loss. DFT calculations incorporating six explicit water molecules around each metal reference ion, with ωB97X-D single-point energy evaluations, favored Pb(II) association but did not reproduce the experimental Cr(III)/Zn(II) ordering. Electronic-state analysis also revealed functional-dependent charge transfer in the Cr-containing model. The results support preferential Pb(II) removal by Cs/GO under the tested competitive conditions and highlight the importance of solution controls, hydration models, and electronic-state assessment when relating calculated metal binding to experimental adsorption behavior.

item.title: Gold Nanoparticles Stabilized by TEMPO-Oxidized Cellulose Nanofibers: Improved Redispersion and Colloidal Stability toward Sensing Platforms
item.description:
Abstract
Gold nanoparticles stabilized by TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers, AuNP-TEMPO, have emerged as promising sustainable nanomaterials, but their colloidal stability and integration into well-defined electroactive architectures for technological applications remain challenging. Here, AuNP-TEMPO were synthesized and subjected to a mild alkaline washing step to improve their macroscopic redispersion behavior and aqueous homogeneity for sensing applications. FTIR and UV–vis analyses indicated changes in AuNP-TEMPO surface chemistry after washing, consistent with deprotonation of carboxylic groups and modulation of the plasmonic response, while TEM confirmed the formation of well-dispersed nanoparticles within a cellulose-derived matrix. The washed AuNP-TEMPO suspension was then combined with chitosan to produce multilayer films by the layer-by-layer (LbL) method. Compared with casting films, the LbL architecture provided better structural organization and controlled buildup, as evidenced by FTIR and UV–vis measurements. Electrochemical characterization showed that increasing the number of bilayers enhanced the amount of electrochemically accessible gold, with the 30-bilayer film exhibiting the best performance. This film was then applied to Cu2+ detection using linear sweep anodic stripping voltammetry, showing a concentration-dependent response with two linear ranges, 10 to 100 ppb and 200 to 400 ppb, and limits of detection of 0.54 and 3.0 ppb, respectively. Taken together, these results indicate that AuNP-TEMPO/chitosan multilayers constitute renewable and tunable electroactive interfaces with promising potential for copper stripping detection.

item.title: Boosting CO 2 Foam Flooding Performance with Tailored CO 2 -Soluble Fluorinated Surfactants AC18xHFPODA/TA
item.description:
Abstract
CO2 foams generated with water-soluble surfactants are often limited by substantial adsorption losses, poor long-distance transport, and insufficient foam generation in deep reservoir regions. Herein, a series of CO2-soluble fluorinated surfactants, denoted as AC18xHFPODA/TA (where AC = C18 alkyl chain, x = EO chain length, HFPO = hexafluoropropylene oxide oligomer, and DA/TA denote the HFPO dimer and trimer segments, respectively), were synthesized by grafting short-chain fluorinated ether segments derived from hexafluoropropylene oxide oligomers onto an alkylamine polyoxyethylene ether backbone through a molecular hybridization strategy. The chemical structures of the synthesized products were determined by FT-IR, 1H NMR, and 19F NMR spectra. The effects of fluorinated-chain, polyoxyethylene-chain, and alkyl-chain lengths on foaming performance were then systematically evaluated to clarify the relationship between molecular structure and foam-regulating properties. The results showed that incorporation of the fluorinated segments significantly improved CO2 solubility and interfacial activity, while also enhancing adsorption and interfacial stabilization at the CO2/water interface. Among the synthesized surfactants, AC1815HFPODA exhibited the best overall performance, with the critical micelle concentration of 0.158 mmol/L and the corresponding surface tension of 28.68 mN/m (at 25 °C), and the cloud-point pressure of 26.75 MPa with concentration of 2.5 wt % at 50 °C. Core flooding experiments further demonstrated that AC1815HFPODA could comigrate with the CO2 phase and generate stable foams in-situ upon contacting the aqueous phase, increasing the resistance factor to 31.86 and substantially improving CO2 mobility control. The generated foam mitigated gas channeling along preferential flow paths by increasing the apparent viscosity of the gas phase and strengthening the Jamin effect within pore throats, thereby improving the potential of foam-based strategies for deep-reservoir mobility control. These findings provide a solid experimental basis for the molecular design of CO2-soluble fluorinated surfactants and support their potential application in CO2 foam flooding.

item.title: Coexposure to Regulated and Unregulated Organohalogens through Omega-3 Fish Oil Supplements: A Retrospective Screening of Products Purchased in 2014–2017
item.description:
Abstract
Omega-3 fish oil supplements are nutraceuticals widely recommended for long-term daily consumption. However, they may also carry bioaccumulative and lipophilic pollutants, and for supplements sold in Latin America the co-occurrence of anthropogenic residues with naturally produced organobromines remains uncharacterized. We therefore determined 23 polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), including 11 dioxin-like congeners (dl-PCBs), seven polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), eight natural methoxylated PBDEs (MeO-BDEs), and total mercury (HgT) in 47 supplements purchased in Brazil and abroad in 2014–2017 and reassessed exposure retrospectively under the 2022 WHO toxic equivalency factors and the 2026 EFSA tolerable intake for dioxins and dl-PCBs (0.6 pg TEQ kg–1 week–1). MeO-BDEs were quantified in all products and dominated the organobromine burden (median ∑MeO-BDE:∑PBDE ≈ 4), yet no widely adopted health-based guidance value exists for them. On a quantified-only, lower-bound screening basis pending confirmatory analysis, six products exceeded the current tolerable intake for dl-PCBs at the label-recommended dose, four of them by more than 3-fold and the highest by 19-fold. Only the most contaminated product exceeded the value in force at the time of purchase (14 pg TEQ kg–1 week–1). PBDEs and MeO-BDEs covaried at the brand level (Spearman ρ = 0.40), a pattern compatible with a shared marine driver whose origin the data do not resolve. All 15 products bearing contaminant-absence statements contained quantifiable contaminants, although the unrecorded scope of those statements precludes any conclusion about their accuracy. These historical data provide a baseline for coexposure to regulated toxicants and to ubiquitous natural organobromines that still lack toxicological guidance.

item.title: Distribution of Calcium Carbonate Polymorphs upon Carbonation of Oil-Well Portland Cement under Geological Conditions
item.description:
Abstract
In oilwells CO2 reacts with Portland cement, inducing portlandite dissolution and C–S–H decalcification, which reduce compressive strength and increase permeability, thereby compromising zonal isolation and wellbore integrity. From a different perspective, the integrity of oil wells may be leveraged due to the autogenous self-healing of cement in CO2-rich environments. Regardless of the approach, it is of paramount importance to understand the progression of carbonation under geological conditions and analyze the associated distribution of calcium carbonate polymorphs due to their distinct stabilities. To that end, in the present study, X-ray microtomography (microCT) has been employed in conjunction with thermogravimetry (TGA) to investigate the progress of carbonation on samples subjected to CO2 attack at 2,000 psi and 60 °C for 14 and 28 days. In the case of a low-density cement matrix (water-to-cement ratio = 0.45), the volume of CaCO3 departs greatly from the volume of the specimen affected by the CO2 attack. On the other hand, in high-density specimens (water-to-cement ratio = 0.35) the volume of formed CaCO3 is substantially closer to that of the affected sample. These results are explained by the porosity of cement matrices. Low-density matrices (thus highly porous) allow extensive permeation of CO2 leading to CaCO3 precipitation, whereas high-density specimens (thus with low porosity) were found to resist CO2 attack to some extent. Finally, the proportion of CaCO3 polymorphs was found to depend on the porosity of the sample and CO2 penetration, a result explained in terms of kinetic and thermodynamic products.

item.title: Atomic-Scale Engineering of Single-Layer hBN through Pd and Pt Decoration: A Density Functional Theory Study
item.description:
Abstract
Metallic seed layers and fabrication-induced defects can significantly influence the properties of two-dimensional electronic devices. We investigate their effects on the electronic properties of atomically thin single-layer hBN and single- and four-atom Pd- and Pt-decorated single-layer hBN models. Density functional theory is used to study the structural stability, charge transfer, polarization, electronic structure, work function, tunneling characteristics, optical response, hydrogen adsorption, and the effects of external electric fields. We find that the Pt-decorated one has stronger binding and a higher tunneling probability than the Pd-decorated one, whereas the latter induces a larger out-of-plane polarization. These results provide atomistic insights into how metallic adatoms and displaced N atoms following vacancy formation affect the electronic properties of atomically thin materials. Such quantitative understanding is important for establishing design guidelines for reliable nanoelectronic devices.

item.title: The Aporphine Alkaloid Dicentrine and Its N-Oxide Derivatives Inhibit Akt Pathway in Head and Neck Cancer Cell Lines and Induce Anti-Inflammatory Response Independent of TP53 Status
item.description:
Abstract
Head and neck squamous cancers (HNSC) are a group of heterogeneous tumors that frequently have TP53 mutations associated with a worse prognosis and poor response to treatment. Current therapy combines chemotherapy and radiotherapy for both early and advanced diseases, underscoring the need for new drugs to improve conventional therapy. In recent years, natural product research has increasingly focused on the discovery and development of anticancer agents. Dicentrine (1), for example, is an aporphine alkaloid isolated from the leaves of Ocotea puberula. Dicentrine and its N-oxide derivatives (compounds 1a and 1b) have demonstrated cytotoxic activity against tumor cells, highlighting their potential as bioactive natural-product scaffolds. As a continuation of our studies, the present work investigated the antitumor potential of compounds 1, 1a, and 1b in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) cell lines with distinct TP53 statuses, namely, FaDu (TP53 mutant) and SCC143 (TP53 wild-type) cells. In vitro studies through cell viability, colony formation assay, cell death, and in silico analysis through molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that compound 1b has lost its antitumor activity, while compounds 1 and 1a inhibited colony formation, decreased cell viability, and induced cell death independently of TP53 status. We also demonstrated that compounds 1 and 1a decreased HMGB1, IL18, and Akt expression. Our in silico analysis suggested that compounds 1 and 1a adopt a productive binding mode at the AKT1 kinase, whereas p53 is not a stable target. Such findings provide additional evidence for the use of compounds 1 and 1a as therapeutic drugs also for head and neck cancer.

item.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Microplastics in the Tidal Forest of Coastal South India─Characteristics, Aging, and Heavy Metal Adsorption
item.description:
Abstract
Tidal forests are ecologically and economically important due to their tolerance of salty water and soil erosion, as well as their ability to sequester carbon. As ubiquitous environmental pollutants, microplastics (MPs) are invading several ecosystems, including tidal forests. The current study aims to identify and classify MPs and the pollutants they transport, collected from a tidal forest in Kota on the west coast of Karnataka, India. MPs in the size range of 0.1 mm to 5 mm were extracted and characterized under a custom-built laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS)–Raman spectroscopic system to identify the polymer class as well as the surface-adsorbed heavy metals. The Raman analysis identified MPs of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET). The LIBS study confirmed the presence of Fe, Ni, Ti, Cr, and Zn. Furthermore, the contact angle study of the larger MPs confirmed that they originated from diverse sources and had varying residence times across different environments. The study also evaluates the relationships among surface morphology, aging, and the adsorption of heavy metals, providing further insights into other environmental pollutants. The MPs with a lower contact angle exhibited a highly degraded surface and the possible presence of hydrophilic carboxyl groups, whereas the MPs with heavy metal contaminants showed a higher contact angle, as cross-validated by the LIBS study. The partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) classifier, coupled with Raman spectral data, achieved the highest accuracy with 4-fold CV. In contrast, the model failed to classify LIBS data using PLS regression (R2 = 0.55) within the studied range due to random variation in spectral features caused by pollutants.

item.title: Pressure Induced Superconductivity in SrSi 2 : A Theoretical Investigation
item.description:
Abstract
SrSi2 is investigated under hydrostatic pressure to understand its structural stability, electronic properties, and superconducting behavior using density-functional theory and Migdal–Eliashberg formalism. SrSi2 is semimetallic and dynamically stable below 30 GPa. The electronic states near the Fermi level are mainly dominated by Si 3p orbitals, and pressure enhances the density of states, indicating increased electronic delocalization. Phonon calculations confirm pressure-induced stabilization, with low-frequency Si vibrations playing a dominant role in lattice dynamics and electron–phonon coupling. The system exhibits weak conventional superconductivity, with the electron–phonon coupling constant and the superconducting transition temperature increasing with pressure. The calculated Tc increases from 1.351 K at 25 GPa to 1.924 K at 29 GPa. However, both dynamical and mechanical instabilities reappear near 30 GPa, suggesting a pressure-induced structural instability limit for superconductivity in SrSi2.

item.title: Meteoric Origin and Temporal Stability of Sembawang Hot Spring Water in Singapore Revealed by Two-Year Geochemical Monitoring
item.description:
Abstract
Sembawang Hot Spring is the only publicly accessible natural hot spring in Singapore and has attracted increasing attention because of its geothermal potential. Previous hydrogeological investigations and thermal profiling studies have suggested that the hot spring is primarily recharged by meteoric water; however, long-term geochemical observations are still limited. In this study, we conducted a two-year observation of water chemistry and stable water isotopes to further constrain the source of Sembawang Hot Spring water and evaluate its temporal stability. The consistently low δ18O and δ2H values in the spring water support a predominantly meteoric origin, with no evidence for a substantial seawater contribution or extensive water-rock interaction. Comparison with long-term precipitation isotope data suggests that intense rainfall in the year-end wet season may contribute disproportionately to groundwater recharge. In addition, the stable isotopic signatures, the absence of a clear seasonal pattern in water chemistry, and the similarity between our geochemical results and previously reported data suggest that the spring water is buffered against short-term variations in precipitation and recharge. These findings provide direct geochemical evidence for the meteoric origin of Sembawang Hot Spring water and show that its hydrogeochemical composition remains relatively stable despite substantial temporal variations in tropical precipitation.

item.title: Ferroelectricity and Bipolaron-Driven Optoelectronic Behavior of ε-WO 3 Nanoparticles at Room Temperature
item.description:
Abstract
A unique polymorph of tungsten trioxide, the epsilon phase (ε-WO3), has an acentric crystal structure, which suggests it may be ferroelectric in nature. Although typically stable below −43 °C in the bulk, it has been stabilized by our group at RT and above. This study explores the ferroelectric nature and bipolaronic behavior of ε-WO3 at room temperature (RT) for the first time. Nanostructured powders synthesized by flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) are shown to exhibit ferroelectric hysteresis and dipole switching, as confirmed via butterfly-type capacitance–voltage study at 1 MHz frequency, piezo-response force microscopy (PFM), and second harmonic generation (SHG) studies. The ferroelectric dipoles of ε-WO3 respond to electro-optical stimuli by forming a bipolaron. The latter interacts with light, producing a single-layer, all-solid-state blue coloration, namely, “the ferrochromic effect”. Our results lay the groundwork for exploring further the structurally simplest ferroelectric ε-WO3 for potentially transforming the field of optoelectronics.

item.title: Polymer-Mediated Gold Deposition on Magnetic Nanoparticles: Structure–Property Relationships for Ultra-Sensitive Electrochemical Interfaces Detection of Leptospira DNA
item.description:
Abstract
Gold-decorated magnetic particles (GMPs) were successfully synthesized through the coprecipitation of oleic acid-stabilized magnetic particles followed by citrate reduction of HAuCl4. Here, we reported the impact of the polymer on the formation of gold-decorated magnetic particles. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed uniformly distributed gold nanoparticles on the surface of the magnetic cores in GMP, whereas seed-mediated synthesis produced GMP-seed with larger particles due to further reduction and growth of gold on pre-existing gold nanoparticles, and more homogeneously distributed gold nanoparticles. The estimated gold mass fraction increased from 47.35% to 58.67% for GMP-seed1 and GMP-seed2, respectively, confirming increased gold deposition during seed-mediated synthesis. Five polymers aminodextran, poly(acrylic acid), poly(vinyl alcohol), poly(ethylenimine), and poly(vinylpyrrolidone)─were first adsorbed onto the magnetic particles prior to gold deposition to investigate polymer-mediated gold nanoparticle formation. Zeta potential and TEM analyses verified successful polymer coating and gold deposition, with variations in surface charge confirming distinct polymer functionalities. The incorporation of gold-decorated magnetic nanostructures into the electrochemical platform enhanced the measured electrochemical response compared with magnetic particles alone, as supported by the quantitative CV peak-current comparison. The GMPs showed successful functionalization with an ssDNA probe complementary to a conserved Leptospira interrogans gene sequence, enabling selective hybridization-based detection by electrochemical assay. The platform demonstrated detection of Leptospira ssDNA down to the lowest tested concentration of 0.1 ng/mL within 20 min, without cross-reactivity with nontarget DNA, demonstrating potential for rapid, field-deployable leptospirosis diagnostics. This nanobiosensor trades extreme sensitivity for rapid, point-of-care operation without thermal cycling─making it far more viable for field deployment in resource-limited, endemic tropical regions.

item.title: High-Temperature Resistant Sealing Materials from Chitosan-Modified Alkali-Activated Coal Gangue for Mine Fire Prevention
item.description:
Abstract
Coal spontaneous combustion remains a persistent hazard in underground mining, demanding sealing materials that retain structural integrity and low gas permeability under sustained thermal loading. Therefore, this study prepared a cementitious firefighting material by alkali activation of coal gangue and modified with low-dosage chitosan for goaf sealing applications. The formulation for the base aluminosilicate matrix was optimized to a 4:6 mass ratio of coal gangue to ground granulated blast furnace slag, a water-to-precursor ratio of 0.40, an activator modulus of 1.0, and a 6% alkali dosage. To overcome the inherent thermal vulnerability of the conventional alkali-activated materials, chitosan was introduced to coordinate with Ca2+ ions released during activation. FTIR, XRD, and SEM characterizations reveal that this coordination forms an interpenetrating organic–inorganic dual-network that bridges the aluminosilicate matrix. Results indicate that at a low chitosan dosage of 0.5%, the material exhibits an optimal 3-day compressive strength of 11.05 MPa. Following thermal exposure, the coordination cross-links effectively dissipate thermal stress and suppress crack propagation, reducing thermally shrinkage by approximately 40% relative to the unmodified matrix at 600 °C. Although this differential narrows at 800 °C, the modification critically preserves macroscopic integrity throughout the 200–600 °C range where crack suppression is most consequential for sealing performance. Permeability and porosity analyses demonstrate that chitosan modification preserves the sealing capacity primarily by disrupting the connectivity of the thermally damaged pore network, yielding an SDR-estimated permeability as low as 0.03 mD. The material utilizes coal gangue as the dominant precursor and achieves marked thermal-resistance enhancement at low chitosan dosage, offering a scalable and resource-efficient strategy for preventing coal spontaneous combustion in underground coal mines.

item.title: N(CH 3 ) 4 B 5 O 6 (OH) 4 ·H 2 O: An [NH 4 ] + -Analogous Hybrid Borate as a Promising Deep Ultraviolet Birefringent Crystal
item.description:
Abstract
Through rational synthetic design, an ammonium-analogous organic cation has been successfully incorporated into a borate framework to afford an organic–inorganic hybrid borate, N(CH3)4B5O6(OH)4·H2O, which contains hydroxylated fundamental building blocks (FBBs) [B5O6(OH)4]−. The compound was obtained by room-temperature evaporation and exhibits a broad transparency window, with a deep-UV absorption cutoff edge at 197 nm. First-principles calculations further show a wide indirect bandgap of 5.6404 eV and a suitable birefringence (0.041@532 nm), indicating that this material is a promising candidate for deep-UV birefringent crystals. This work underscores that hybrid borates incorporating tetraalkylammonium cations represent a promising platform for exploring novel deep-UV birefringent materials.

item.title: Performance and Emission Characteristics of Apricot Kernel Oil Methyl Ester–Diesel Blends in a Compression Ignition Engine: RSM-Based Multi-Criteria Optimization across Engine Speed Regimes
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, biodiesel (AKOME) produced from apricot kernel oil through the transesterification method was blended with diesel fuel in volumetric ratios of 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% (B5, B10, B15, B20). In a single-cylinder, four-stroke, air-cooled compression ignition (CI) engine, under full load conditions, experiments were conducted at four different engine speeds (1000, 1500, 2000, and 2500 rpm) to measure engine performance parameters (BTE, Torque, Brake Power, BSFC) and exhaust emissions (CO, NO, NOx, HC, EGT). Based on 60 experimental observations (3 repetitions × 4 speeds × 5 blends), the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) models exhibited high prediction accuracy, ranging from R2 = 0.890 (CO) to R2 = 0.976 (BSFC). Sufficient Precision values remained well above the recommended minimum threshold of 4.0 for all response variables (34.98–67.96). The multicriteria optimization conducted using the weighted desirability function (CO × 3, HC × 3, NOx × 2, BTE × 1, BSFC × 1) revealed an optimal blending strategy dependent on engine speed. At 1000 rpm, B20 provided the highest global desirability (D = 0.340), reducing CO by 33.6% and HC by 30.7%, while only increasing BSFC by 4.6%. In the 1500–2000 rpm range, while D100 maintained its marginal superiority, the difference with the closest biodiesel blend remained ΔD < 0.06, indicating practical interchangeability. At high engine speeds of 2500 rpm, D100 was preferred due to the increase in HC caused by the viscosity of biodiesel. B20, across all tested speeds, provided an average CO reduction of 24.1% compared to D100, with the highest reduction measured at 50.1% at 2500 rpm. The obtained results demonstrate that AKOME-diesel mixtures can be directly used in engines without any construction modifications. Additionally, these findings provide a comprehensive biodiesel evaluation framework that enables the development of optimized fuel strategies based on engine operating conditions.

item.title: Physicochemical Characterization, Engine Performance, and Emission Evaluation of Ternary Fuel Blends: Valorizing Agricultural Plastic Pyrolysis Oil and End-of-Life Transformers
item.description:
Abstract
This study presents a systematic investigation of waste agricultural plastic pyrolysis oil (waste plastic oil (WPO)) and waste transformer oil (WTO) as a combined alternative fuel blend for a compression-ignition engine. Agricultural plastic/rubber waste was converted into fuel-grade pyrolysis oil through a novel energy-integrated batch pyrolysis process (1 ton capacity horizontal rotary reactor, 350–450 °C) with a 45% liquid fuel yield. Four fuel blends were prepared and comprehensively characterized: base diesel (D100), a 40% WTO blend (WTO40), a 40% WPO blend (WPO40), and a new ternary blend of 20% WPO +20% WTO (WPO20WTO20). Advanced characterization techniques such as Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) and distillation curve analysis revealed that all blends met ASTM D6751 specifications for density (830–850 kg/m3) and kinematic viscosity (2.84–4.50 mm2/s) and exhibited outstanding cold flow properties (cloud points −6 to −25 °C, pour points −27 to ≤ −40 °C). Engine performance tests were conducted at four engine speeds (1200, 1600, 2000, and 2400 rpm) on a single-cylinder air-cooled diesel engine under full load. With a 12.59% torque increase, a 14.07% brake power (BP) improvement, and a 3.2% brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC) reduction, WPO20WTO20 was the best-performing fuel. Improvements achieved with WTO40 and WPO40 blends were 11.31% and 9.06% increase in torque and 6.2% and 5.6% decrease in BSFC, respectively. WTO40 provided the highest efficiency improvements, and brake thermal efficiency improvements ranged from 3.8% to 6.7% across all fuel blends. Emission analyses revealed that WPO40 reduced carbon monoxide (CO) emission by an average of 37.35%, while WPO20WTO20 caused an increase by 23.81%. Emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx) increased significantly in all blends compared to D100: +51.61% in WTO40, +46.73% in WPO20WTO20, and +45.40% in WPO40, consistent with the elevated aromatic content confirmed by FT-IR analysis. Nevertheless, exhaust gas recirculation and selective catalytic reduction aftertreatment systems have demonstrated potential for addressing such NOx increases in published studies; however, their compatibility and performance with WPO–WTO blend exhaust constituents were not experimentally verified in the present study. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study to systematically characterize ternary WPO–WTO–diesel blends and document double-digit simultaneous improvements in torque (+12.59%) and BP (+14.07%) along with synergistic distillation behavior (32.1% yield in the 250–300 °C range) and arctic-grade cold flow properties. It should be noted that in-cylinder combustion parameters (heat release rate, ignition delay) and CO2/HC emissions were not measured in the present study due to instrumentation constraints; interpretations of combustion behavior are therefore grounded in physicochemical characterization data.

item.title: Multifunctional PMMA 144 - b -PDMAEMA 51 /TiO 2 Nanocomposites for Efficient Dye Removal and Antibacterial Applications: Experimental and DFT Insights
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, poly(methyl methacrylate)-b-poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (PMMA-b-PDMAEMA), an amphiphilic block copolymer containing various chain lengths of a pH- and temperature-responsive PDMAEMA segment, was synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). A PMMA-Br macroinitiator was first prepared by polymerization of methyl methacrylate using butyl 2-bromoisobutyrate (BuBriB) and a CuBr/2,2′-bipyridine catalytic system, and then the chain was extended with further batch polymerization of DMAEMA using the PMMA-Br macroinitiator. TiO2 nanoparticles were synthesized by the sol–gel method, and they were incorporated into the block copolymer through solvent casting to obtain PMMA-b-PDMAEMA/TiO2 nanocomposites. The synthesized copolymers and nanocomposites were comprehensively characterized by GPC, FTIR, 1H NMR, TGA, DSC, SEM, and XRD. The polymer nanocomposite containing 10% TiO2 achieved over 96% removal of methylene blue (MB) within 70 min at pH 7 under visible LED irradiation in the presence of NaBH4. In addition, it exhibited significant antibacterial activity, producing inhibition zones of 24.75 mm against Shigella sonnei (S. sonnei) and 23.25 mm against Staphylococcus hemolyticus(S. hemolyticus) at a dose of 45 μg. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidated the interactions between TiO2 nanoparticles and PMMA-b-PDMAEMA, the adsorption mechanism of methylene blue, and the interactions of the nanocomposites with bacterial cell proteins. These findings demonstrated that PMMA-b-PDMAEMA/TiO2 nanocomposites are promising multifunctional materials for environmental remediation by combining efficient dye adsorption with antibacterial activity. The novelty of this work lies in the development of a multifunctional PMMA-b-PDMAEMA/TiO2 nanocomposite that combines the mechanical stability, pH-responsive behavior, dye adsorption, and antibacterial properties of the prepared nanocomposites on a single platform for environmental remediation.

item.title: One-Step Simultaneous Crystallization of Hydrocalumite and Hydrotalcite-like Materials: Evaluation of Their Uncalcined and Calcined Products on the Photocatalytic Degradation of Toxic Phenolic Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
Simultaneous crystallization of hydrotalcite and hydrocalumite-like compounds was carried out by a one-step coprecipitation method. A nominal molar ratio M2+/M3+ = 2 was established, while the zinc amount varied in the 5–50% mol range. Thermal treatments at 500, 600, and 700 °C were performed. Samples were characterized by X-ray powder diffraction (XRD), diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and N2 physisorption. Likewise, the uncalcined and calcined samples were evaluated in the UV photodegradation of 2,4-dichlorophenol, 4-chlorophenol, and phenol. ZnO and P25-TiO2 were also evaluated for comparison. The simultaneous crystallization of hydrotalcite, hydrocalumite, and ZnO occurred in uncalcined samples, while the coexistence of structurally expanded CaO and Al-doped ZnO was observed in the calcined ones. Also, the band gap values decreased progressively with the annealing temperature and the zinc amount. The best photoactivity was achieved with the calcined solids at 700 °C, specifically the sample with nominal 50% zinc mol percent whose percentages of photodegradation in a lapse time of 3 h were 85% for 2,4-dichlorophenol, 99% for 4-chlorophenol, and 35% for phenol, being higher than ZnO (15% for 2,4-dichlorophenol, 0% for 4-chlorophenol, and 8% for phenol) and TiO2 (52% for 2,4-dichlorophenol, 85% for 4-chlorophenol, and 52% for phenol). Mineralization percentages were also higher than ZnO and TiO2. The reutilization study revealed that samples maintained their activity up to the third cycle, and catalyst deactivation was caused by calcium leaching. It was verified that by controlling the zinc content and the annealing temperature, the structural, textural, optical, and catalytic performance can be adjusted, yielding high photoactive materials.

item.title: Cobalt-Regulated Selenium Conversion Chemistry in Two-Dimensional Carbon for Fast and Durable Potassium–Selenium Batteries
item.description:
Abstract
Potassium–selenium batteries are attractive for high-energy, cost-effective energy storage, yet their practical performance is constrained by sluggish K–Se conversion kinetics, poor electronic conductivity of Se, and dissolution/migration of soluble potassium polyselenides. Herein, a cobalt nanoparticle-regulated two-dimensional carbon host is developed to construct a Se@Co/2D-C cathode with integrated catalytic, conductive, and anchoring functions. The embedded metallic Co nanoparticles promote the formation of graphitic domains, enhance electronic transport, and induce local charge modulation to accelerate Se–K reaction kinetics. Meanwhile, the Co sites effectively immobilize potassium polyselenide intermediates, mitigating active-material loss during cycling. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, Se@Co/2D-C delivers a high initial reversible capacity of 665.9 mAh g–1 with an initial Coulombic efficiency of 77.8% at 0.1 A g–1. It also exhibits excellent rate capability, retaining 513 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1, and outstanding long-term durability with 498.1 mAh g–1 after 2000 cycles. Kinetic analyses further confirm enhanced capacitive contribution, faster K+ diffusion, and reduced charge-transfer resistance. This work highlights transition-metal-mediated catalytic regulation as a promising route toward durable, fast-kinetic Se cathodes for practical K–Se batteries.

item.title: Potential of an LRG1-Targeting Degrader in Combating Aggressive Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains clinically challenging due to its aggressive phenotype and the scarcity of druggable targets. Leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) is a critical driver of TNBC progression, yet its has precluded the development of conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. In this study, we employed an event-driven proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) strategy to target this “undruggable” LRG1 for degradation. Leveraging our previously developed ETTAC-2─a peptide-based PROTAC with established efficacy in ocular neovascularization and renal fibrosis models─we demonstrate that this degrader induces effective LRG1 degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system in a dose- and time-dependent manner in 4T1 TNBC cells. Mechanistically, ETTAC-2-mediated degradation of LRG1 suppressed the p-AKT and HIF-1α signaling axes, impairing cell proliferation in vitro and orchestrating a robust antitumor response in vivo. Systemic administration of ETTAC-2 significantly attenuated mammary tumor growth and impeded the aggressive phenotype by reversing the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) program through sustained inhibition of HIF-1α signaling. By effectively reversing EMT markers and curtailing the malignant progression of TNBC without observable systemic toxicity, our findings validate LRG1 as a viable therapeutic target and establish ETTAC-2 as a pioneering lead compound that bypasses structural limitations to treat recalcitrant breast cancers.

item.title: Effects of Resistance Compensation on Laser-Induced Graphene Electrodes
item.description:
Abstract
Laser-induced graphene (LIG) offers a promising approach for fabricating low-cost, flexible, and disposable electrochemical sensors. However, the electrical resistance associated with thin conductive tracks and their connections can introduce substantial ohmic potential losses, compromising potential control and distorting electrochemical measurements. Here, we report a paper-based LIG electrochemical platform incorporating a four-terminal configuration designed to minimize resistance-related distortions through separate current-carrying and potential-sensing pathways. The electrodes were fabricated by direct CO2 laser scribing of Kraft paper, producing a porous, graphene-like carbon network characterized by scanning electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy. The electrochemical effects of resistance compensation were systematically investigated using cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy with ferricyanide/ferrocyanide, hexaammineruthenium, dopamine, and paracetamol. Resistance compensation substantially improved voltammetric peak definition and potential control, shifting the dopamine oxidation peak from 0.70 to 0.40 V and reducing the fitted uncompensated series resistance from 197 to 35 Ω for hexaammineruthenium. In contrast, the charge-transfer resistance remained nearly unchanged, indicating that the observed improvements primarily resulted from reduced ohmic distortions rather than changes in intrinsic electron-transfer kinetics. Under resistance-compensated conditions, the LIG electrodes enabled dopamine determination over 120–900 μmol L–1, with a detection limit of 29 μmol L–1, and paracetamol determination over 125–1660 μmol L–1, with a detection limit of 37 μmol L–1, using cyclic voltammetry. Differential pulse voltammetry further improved paracetamol detection, achieving a detection limit of 2.5 μmol L–1 over a linear range of 10–60 μmol L–1. The proposed platform was successfully applied to paracetamol determination in commercial pharmaceutical tablets, providing a recovery of 93%, in close agreement with the 94% obtained by high-performance liquid chromatography. The integration of laser-based fabrication and resistance compensation provides a practical strategy for minimizing measurement artifacts and improving the reliability of low-cost, paper-based electrochemical sensors.

item.title: TRACE-Net: A Physics-Inspired Geometric Deep Learning Framework for Antibody–Antigen Docking Ranking
item.description:
Abstract
Elucidating antibody–antigen interactions at atomic resolution is fundamental for therapeutic antibody design. However, accurately discriminating near-native conformations from massive decoy pools remains a critical bottleneck for current high-accuracy structure prediction, as existing scoring functions often fail to capture complex interfacial interactions and monomeric deformation. To address this challenge, we present TRACE-Net, a physics-inspired geometric deep learning framework. TRACE-Net introduces three innovative modules: Context-Aware Edge Feature Recalibration (CEER), Internal Deformation-Aware Gated Fusion (IDGF), and Top-Weighted Combined Ranking Loss (TWCRL). Trained on a comprehensive data set of 1442 complexes, the model effectively reduces geometric noise and quantifies spatial divergence as a structural indicator of localized geometric deformation forced during flexible interface adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that TRACE-Net effectively mitigates the severe ranking inversion of near-native decoys, yielding a competitive improvement in the Top-1 success rate, particularly on challenging targets. Overall, this framework offers a sensitive and informative scoring strategy for assessing predicted structures and advancing computational immunology.

item.title: Valorization of Sawdust into Functional Cellulose–Alginate Materials as Hemostatic Composites
item.description:
Abstract
This study aimed to valorize waste-derived microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) from black pine sawdust into calcium–alginate-cross-linked composites as candidate hemostatic materials. MCC was extracted by combining alkali-sodium dodecyl sulfate treatment and NaClO/H2O2 bleaching, then cross-linked with sodium alginate at cellulose/alginate ratios of 25:75, 50:50, and 75:25 (w/w) in the presence of CaCl2 and freeze-dried into porous scaffolds. Raman spectroscopy identified the extracted cellulose as MCC with 93.5% similarity to reference spectra, while cellulose and alginate functional groups and Ca2+ mediated cross-linking were confirmed by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. X-ray diffractograms showed that the crystallinity index (CrI) fell from 13.3 to 3.7% as the alginate content increased. Quantitative analysis of scanning electron microscopy (SEM) micrographs showed that pore number density decreased from 96 pores/mm2 for pure MCC to 37 pores/mm2 for 25MCC75ALG, reflecting a shift from numerous narrow interfiber gaps to fewer, wider cavities as the alginate content increased, whereas the open-pore area fraction remained statistically similar among formulations (53–66%). The decrease in pore density paralleled the increase in water-holding capacity (WHC) from ∼3–4 to ∼50. Clotting assays with human blood showed that the most hydrating composites (25MCC75ALG and 50MCC50ALG) reduced clotting time to ∼80–100 s, compared with ∼194 s for pure MCC and ∼337 s for untreated blood. The results demonstrated a route for transforming forestry waste into functional biomaterials whose crystallinity, porosity, and hydration could be tuned through the MCC/alginate ratio for potential biomedical applications.

item.title: Biodegradable Cu/Sr Co-Doped Hydroxyapatite Composite for Bone Defect Reconstruction: An In Vivo Study
item.description:
Abstract
Bone defect repair remains a significant challenge in the clinic, particularly in complex ischemic situations. Conventional bone substitutes typically fail due to defect geometries, impaired blood supply, or unbalanced degradation in coordination with new bone formation. To address these limitations, we developed a bioactive, injectable bone void filler. It consists of a poly(vinyl alcohol)/sodium alginate (PVA/SA) composite loaded with copper (Cu), strontium (Sr), and codoped with low-crystallinity hydroxyapatite (HA) granules. Specifically, HA codoped with 1 mol % Cu and 4 mol % Sr was hydrothermally synthesized at 120 °C and incorporated into a double-network PVA/SA hydrogel. The regenerative capacity of this composite was then evaluated by implanting preformed cylinders into a nonload-bearing rat femoral defect model for 4 and 8 weeks. Bone regeneration and neovascularization were assessed using micro-CT and immunohistology. In vivo tests demonstrated that this composite is replaced by bone. Micro-CT and histological evaluations of the in vivo results showed that the Cu/Sr codoped composite enhanced bone defect repair accompanied by enhanced early neovascularization, supporting coordinated vascular and bone tissue regeneration. Lastly, histological staining revealed unique healing patterns characterized by “bridge-like” bone restoration and “island-like” regeneration, offering a promising option for treating complex bone defects.

item.title: Small Molecules Engineered to Trigger Virus-like Particle Disassembly
item.description:
Abstract
A molecular delivery system needs to release, as well as package, cargo. In previous work, technology has been described for packaging cargo into virus-like particles (VLPs) based on the Hepatitis B Virus capsid. Here, we describe a panel of dansyl maleimides (DM) designed to trigger VLP disassembly in response to a reducing environment. The VLP is stabilized by protein–protein interactions and also disulfide cross-links between the C-terminal cysteine of each capsid protein (Cp). The DM molecules react with a second cysteine, buried at the Cp-Cp interface. The DMs, of varying size, disrupt Cp-Cp interactions, leaving VLPs held together primarily by disulfide cross-links. Introduction of β-mercaptoethanol (βME), emulating the reducing environment of the cytoplasm, results in the disassembly of the DM-labeled VLPs. The most effective DM binds VLPs slowly, destabilizes them more than other DMs, and leads to rapid disassembly; with this DM, labeling as few as 50% of available sites led to disassembly. Cargo-loaded DM-labeled VLPs also showed complete disassembly when incubated with βME. This work outlines a strategy for future development of VLPs as nanocontainers that are responsive to the environment.

item.title: Cross-Stream Thermocapillary Migration of a Droplet in a Confined Oscillatory Flow
item.description:
Abstract
The study of cross-stream migration of droplets in a confined oscillatory flow turns out to be of significant importance in various physiological systems. Although significant exploration has been done on the thermocapillary migration of droplets in a pressure-driven flow, a linear superposition of time-dependent flow oscillations would not be suitable to address the nonlinearity due to channel confinement and interfacial deformation. The present study numerically investigates the role of an externally imposed temperature gradient on the manipulation of droplets suspended in such a flow field. The effect of channel confinement and flow-induced shape deformation is also presented. It is observed that a droplet, suspended in an oscillatory imposed flow, exhibits cross-stream migration toward the upper hot wall at a comparatively lower imposed lateral temperature gradient than in a system without any flow pulsation. The numerical model presented herein offers a robust framework for droplet manipulation in a nonisothermal oscillatory flow field and has significant applications in different biomicrofluidic applications with an imposed oscillatory flow.

item.title: A Binuclear Ruthenium–Phenformin Compound: Synthesis, Characterization, and Inhibition of the DHFR Enzyme
item.description:
Abstract
The Ru-phenformin compound Ru80 was synthesized and characterized by NMR and UV/Vis spectroscopies, as well as by SCXRD, HRMS, and elemental analysis. Enzymatic assays confirm that Ru80 is effective in reducing the catalytic activity of DHFR enzyme. Ru80 retains its inhibitory activity under macromolecularly crowded conditions designed to mimic cellular environments, requiring slightly higher concentrations to achieve comparable levels of inhibition. Thermodynamic analysis demonstrates that Ru80 significantly weakens the binding affinity of NADPH cofactor to DHFR enzyme. Enzyme kinetic analysis also suggests a mixed (noncompetitive) inhibition mechanism where Ru80 binds to the free enzyme as well as the enzyme substrate complex. Ru80 binds to DHFR enzyme in a time-dependent and nonspecific manner.

item.title: Transfer Learning with Graph Neural Networks for Experimental Prediction of Organic Photovoltaic Efficiency
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a transfer learning approach that enhances power conversion efficiency (PCE) predictions in organic photovoltaics (OPVs) by resolving the critical issue of missing descriptors in real-world databases. Specifically, we address the challenge of missing frontier molecular orbital descriptors (HOMO and LUMO) within an extensive data set of 1346 experimental OPV records established by the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology (KRICT). To resolve this, a graph neural network (GNN) was pretrained on 100,000 computational molecules from the Harvard Clean Energy Project (CEP). Crucially, this model was utilized to impute the missing experimental HOMO/LUMO levels, effectively bridging the computational–experimental domain gap. By incorporating these successfully imputed electronic descriptors with device-level processing parameters, we achieved relative R2 gains of approximately 8–25% across most machine learning models, with Random Forest yielding the top performance (R2 = 0.837). By integrating GNN-based representation learning with transfer learning from experimental data, the proposed approach is not restricted to specific regression models and can be extended to various molecular- and device-level properties as a framework, providing a flexible and data-efficient strategy for the design of high-performance OPV systems.

item.title: Synthesis, Computational Evaluation, and Anticancer Assessment of Benzofuran-Based Pyrano[2,3- c ]pyrazole Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
A new series of benzofuran-based pyrano[2,3-c]pyrazole derivatives 4a–e was synthesized and evaluated through integrated synthetic, computational, and biological studies. The target compounds were prepared via a multistep route involving Sonogashira coupling, iodine-mediated cyclization, Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, and final K2CO3-mediated one-pot cyclocondensation under mild reaction conditions. The optimized protocol afforded the desired derivatives in high to excellent yields (88–98%), and their structures were confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS analyses. ADMET prediction indicated acceptable drug-likeness profiles, favorable intestinal permeability, and low predicted toxicity risks for the synthesized derivatives. Molecular docking studies against CDK2, the androgen receptor, VEGFR2, and Bcl-2 yielded favorable docking scores and predicted ligand-residue interactions within the selected binding pockets. Among the synthesized compounds, 4c showed the most favorable docking scores toward CDK2 and the androgen receptor, whereas 4a showed the most favorable scores toward VEGFR2 and Bcl-2. The most favorable complexes obtained from molecular docking were further examined by 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, where RMSD, RMSF, and Rg analyses supported their dynamic stability and structural compactness during the simulation period. Biological evaluation demonstrated moderate, cell line-dependent antiproliferative activity, with 4a showing the lowest EC50 values against A549 and LNCaP cells (75.58 and 86.40 μM, respectively). Mechanistic assays indicated that the active derivatives promoted apoptosis, regulated apoptosis-related gene expression, suppressed cell migration and colony formation, enhanced intracellular ROS generation, disrupted mitochondrial membrane potential, and affected cell-cycle progression. These findings suggest that benzofuran-based pyrano[2,3-c]pyrazoles represent biologically relevant heterocyclic scaffolds with measurable anticancer activity supported by computational and cellular evidence.

item.title: Direct Phosphate Triester Synthesis via Condensation of Phosphoric Acid with Alcohols and Unsymmetrical Phosphate Triester Synthesis via Esterification of Diaryl Phosphates
item.description:
Abstract
Phosphorus is a critical element for agriculture and industrial applications, but it is finite and geographically localized. This study addresses the challenge of phosphorus resource depletion by developing a direct triesterification method for ubiquitously available phosphoric acid, thereby bypassing the use of white phosphorus. We demonstrate that phosphoric acid can be directly converted into phosphate triesters using alcohols and N,N-dimethylformamide. The reaction exhibited a substrate scope for primary saturated and unsaturated aliphatic alcohols in isolated yields of 39–94%, whereas secondary alcohols, low-boiling alcohols, phenol, and benzyl alcohol showed limitations. This approach was further extended to the synthesis of unsymmetrical phosphate triesters from diaryl phosphate diesters, and monoalkyl diaryl phosphates were obtained in isolated yields of 23–58%. Overall, this study offers a practical and resource-conscious alternative for the direct synthesis of industrially valuable phosphate triesters from phosphoric acid, thereby reducing the reliance on phosphate rock or white phosphorus.

item.title: Unraveling SAF Supply Chains: A Global Assessment of CORSIA-Certified Lipid-Based Biomass
item.description:
Abstract
The decarbonization of civil aviation remains one of the most complex challenges in the global energy transition, given the sector’s reliance on high-energy-density liquid fuels and the limited prospects for large-scale electrification. Within this context, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) represents the most immediately deployable mitigation option. However, the scalability of SAF is strongly constrained by feedstock availability, sustainability certification, and technological maturity. This review provides a critical and integrated assessment of lipid-based biomass certified under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), focusing on their chemical composition, technological conversion routes, greenhouse gas mitigation potential, and global production capacity. Eighteen oleaginous feedstocks, including vegetable oils, animal fats, processing residues, and waste-derived lipids, are systematically evaluated by correlating compositional attributes, impurity levels, seasonality, and logistics with conversion performance and Technology Readiness Levels. Particular emphasis is placed on the dominance of the hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids pathway, which currently represents the most mature and commercially viable route for SAF production. The analysis demonstrates that second-generation feedstocks, especially residual and waste lipids, consistently outperform dedicated crops, achieving life-cycle greenhouse gas reductions of up to 80–90% relative to fossil jet fuel while minimizing land-use change impacts.

item.title: Melt-Processed Biodegradable Cellulose Nanofibrils–Thermoplastic Starch Composites for Enhanced-Efficiency Monoammonium Phosphate Fertilizers
item.description:
Abstract
The increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices requires environmentally friendly technologies that improve nutrient use efficiency while reducing environmental losses.
